titre: Huntington's (1983): Locating a Gene Before Knowing It
accroche: In 1983, a DNA marker linked to Huntington's disease is placed on chromosome 4. The gene itself was isolated only in 1993.
contenu_vulgarise:
In the mid-1950s, the Venezuelan physician Americo Negrette spends a year of national service in San Luis, near Lake Maracaibo. There he observes residents who tremble as if they were drunk. Neighbors call it “el mal de San Vito.” Negrette records the family history, notes transmission from generation to generation, and concludes that it is Huntington's chorea, described in 1872 by George Huntington.

The population of Lake Maracaibo is the largest known for this disease. According to Bhattacharyya (2016), its sufferers descend from a single woman, María Concepción Soto, who lived there in the early 18th century. In 1972, for the centenary of Huntington's description, Ramón Ávila-Girón presents recordings of these patients in New York. Nancy Wexler, whose mother is affected, then organizes missions to Venezuela, beginning in July 1979. The survey, carried out over twenty years, documents 18,000 people in order to establish a common genealogy.

## A marker, not a gene

In November 1983, the journal Nature publishes the paper by James Gusella, Nancy Wexler, and twelve other coauthors: “A polymorphic DNA marker genetically linked to Huntington's disease.” The abstract fits in two sentences. Family studies show that the disease gene is linked to a polymorphic DNA marker located on chromosome 4. The localization is presented as the first step toward identifying the primary genetic defect.

A polymorphic marker is, to a first approximation, a DNA fragment that exists in several variants from one person to another. If, within a family, a variant is passed on with the disease far more often than chance explains, the gene lies near the marker on the chromosome. The variant involved may change from one family to another. One can thus locate a gene without knowing anything about what it does, or about the protein it makes.

## It is not yet the gene

It would be inaccurate to say that the Huntington's disease gene was isolated in 1983. One must wait until 1993 and a paper by the Huntington's Disease Collaborative Research Group in the journal Cell: “A novel gene containing a trinucleotide repeat that is expanded and unstable on Huntington's disease chromosomes.” The title states the nature of the anomaly: a repeat of three DNA letters, lengthened and unstable.

## A test before the gene

The 1983 approach is the reverse of the usual one. At the start, no suspect protein, no suspected function: a map, then a neighborhood to explore. Ten years separate the map from the gene.

During those ten years, medicine did not wait. According to Bhattacharyya, a presymptomatic and prenatal test for the disease has been available worldwide since 1986. Nancy Wexler directed a program that offered it, and never wanted to know her own result. She compared the test to a crystal ball that shows the future.

Seven years before the gene was isolated, a test already existed: it just couldn't yet read the anomaly itself.

repere.texte: According to the abstract of the 1983 paper, family studies show that the Huntington's disease gene is linked to a polymorphic DNA marker located on human chromosome 4.
repere.source: Gusella et al., “A polymorphic DNA marker genetically linked to Huntington's disease,” Nature, 306, 1983

carte.punch: In 1983, the Huntington's gene is located on chromosome 4. It will be isolated only in 1993.
carte.idee: The 1983 paper by Gusella, Wexler, and their coauthors links Huntington's disease to a DNA marker on chromosome 4. This is a localization, not the isolation of the gene: that dates from 1993 and reveals a repeat of three DNA letters, lengthened and unstable.

quiz.question: What exactly does the 1983 paper by Gusella and his coauthors establish?
choix: That the disease comes from an unstable repeat of three DNA letters
That the protein involved functions in the neurons of the cortex
That the disease gene is located on the X chromosome
That the gene is linked to a polymorphic DNA marker on chromosome 4
quiz.explication: The paper locates the gene by linkage with a DNA marker, without isolating it, and places it on chromosome 4, not on the X. The repeat of three letters comes from the 1993 paper, and the function of the protein is not known in 1983.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Which peculiarity of the gene does the 1993 paper by the Huntington's Disease Collaborative Research Group reveal?
choix: A repeat of three DNA letters, lengthened and unstable
An extra copy of the gene in all patients
A total loss of the gene in patients
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The paper's title speaks of a gene containing a trinucleotide repeat, expanded and unstable on the patients' chromosomes. The title mentions neither loss of the gene, nor deletion of the chromosome, nor an extra copy.

quiz_supplementaire.question: According to Bhattacharyya, since when has a presymptomatic and prenatal test for Huntington's disease been available worldwide?
choix: Since 1972, the year of the New York presentation of the patients
Since 1993, the year the gene itself was isolated
Since 1986, seven years before the gene was isolated
Since 1979, the year of Wexler's first missions to Venezuela
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Bhattacharyya places the availability of the presymptomatic and prenatal test in 1986, seven years after Wexler's 1979 missions and seven years before the gene itself was isolated, in 1993; 1972 is the date of the New York presentation of the patients, not that of the test.
